g.text: Name:
Date:
OCT
Small actions can help communities
What clue would you check first on October 17?
Have you ever wondered why a small calendar box can open a much bigger
story? On October 17, October 17 is a day for learning how communities
can work together to reduce poverty. This is a recurring observance or a
year-independent fact, so the class keeps the calendar day 17 as the
main date clue and uses 2017 only for a pretend timeline. The title card
says “Small actions can help communities,” and it invites readers to
look for the problem, invention, creature, or challenge behind the
headline. A history detective does not need to memorize every detail;
the detective notices which clues can be checked and which numbers can
be used carefully. In this classroom version, the event-year clue ends
in 1; for the worksheet, each museum panel gets 3 labels, and the
display repeats that set across 4 panels. The passage also names 2 clues
that can be set aside after the first round. The timeline comparison
uses 2017 and a gap of 4 years, while the October label 17 helps us
connect the math back to the story. The source is United Nations, so the
event claim is not invented for the worksheet. After reading, ask what
you would check first, whether the display tells the same story, and how
a number can describe a real event without becoming the whole event.
History becomes easier to remember when a reader asks a question, checks
a source, and then explains the clue in their own words.
